title: Conditional Sentences: Hindi to English Practice — Practice Work 1
content:
## Conditional Sentences: Hindi to English Practice

Use conditional sentences to translate a connected set of ideas from Hindi into English.

### Lesson focus

1. If it rains, the crop will be good.
2. If the crop is good, I will get some money.
3. If I get some money, I will build a shed/room for the animals.

### Understand the pattern

A chain of first conditionals can link several possible future events. Each if-clause uses present simple even though the overall story concerns the future. The result clause normally uses will plus a base verb.

### Worked answers and explanation

If it rains, the crop will be good. If the crop is good, I will receive some money. If I receive some money, I will build a shelter for the animals. Each result supplies the next condition; these are possibilities rather than promises that every step will happen.

### Try another

Extend the chain: If I build a shelter, the animals ___. (stay dry)

### Suggested answer

Will stay dry is a suitable result. The new if-clause uses build, not will build; the result uses will stay.
